title: Arrokoth
subtitle: The most distant world explored

description:
Episode 84 of a daily journey through the universe. ⛄
Arrokoth: on January 1, 2019, NASA's New Horizons flew past this 36-km Kuiper Belt object, the most distant object ever explored up close. Two lobes that gently touched 4.5 billion years ago: a time capsule from the birth of the planets.

segments.text: In twenty fifteen, NASA's New Horizons spacecraft flew past Pluto. But its journey wasn't over.
segments.headline: After Pluto

segments.text: It kept going, deeper into the Kuiper belt, toward a small icy world no one had ever seen up close.
segments.headline: Deeper into the dark

segments.text: On January first, twenty nineteen, it flew past Arrokoth, the most distant object ever explored up close.
It's about thirty-six kilometers long and looks like a flattened snowman: two lobes stuck together.
segments.headline: A cosmic snowman

segments.text: The two pieces didn't crash. They drifted together gently, at walking speed, and stuck.
segments.headline: A gentle touch

segments.text: It's red, coated with organic compounds cooked by billions of years of faint sunlight and cosmic rays.
segments.headline: Red and frozen

segments.text: It has barely changed since the planets formed, about four and a half billion years ago.
Arrokoth means sky in the Powhatan language. It's a frozen time capsule from the birth of our solar system.
segments.headline: A time capsule

segments.text: Tomorrow, a golden record carrying Earth's sounds and music to the stars. Next stop: the Golden Record. Follow, so you don't miss episode eighty-five.
